title: Security review: data residency & region pinning - Atlas Health
summary: High-level security review focused on data residency and region pinning requirements for Atlas Health. Discussed options for EU-only processing, cross-border telemetry, subprocessors (cloud providers), contractual controls (DPA/SCCs), BYOK/KMS patterns, audit logs retention, and proof points (SOC 2). Agreed next steps: share SOC2 + DPA, provide region-pinning architecture diagram, run a short demo of EU-only routing, and confirm custodial KMS options.
next_steps: Jordan Park: Share SOC 2 Type II report, DPA draft, and list of subprocessors by 2025-03-14
Samira Khan: Prepare and record a 10-min EU-region pinning demo (test tenant) by 2025-03-19
Lina Gomez: Send list of workloads that must remain inside EU by 2025-03-17
Peter Novak & Samira: Schedule follow-up deep dive on KMS/BYOK integration week of 2025-03-24
action_items: Jordan Park: email SOC2 and DPA + subprocessors spreadsheet (due 2025-03-14)
Samira Khan: spin up EU-only routing demo and video (due 2025-03-19)
Lina Gomez: enumerate EU-bound endpoints and compliance requirements (due 2025-03-17)
Arjun Patel: confirm encryption key management requirements (BYOK/HSM) and share internal policy (due 2025-03-20)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Location: Zoom link | Attendees: Jordan Park, Samira Khan, Naomi Chen (Redwood) -- Maya Lopez, Arjun Patel, Lina Gomez, Peter Novak (Atlas) 

Summary (auto): Quick recap of Atlas's data residency musts; deep dive on region pinning and cross-border processing; KMS and audit logs; next steps to demonstrate EU-only routing and share SOC2/DPA docs. 

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Park from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, with Samira and Naomi. How are you all doing? 
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. Busy, but excited to go through the residency part, this is the main blocker before procurement. 
[00:15] Jordan: Totally understood. The goal today is to show how we can guarantee EU-only processing for patient data, call out exceptions, and surface controls like BYOK, audit logs, and subprocessors. 
[00:28] Samira: Quick agenda — architecture for region pinning, what crosses borders (if anything), KMS options, audit/retention, and contract items (DPA, SCCs). 
[00:38] Arjun: For compliance, we need a clear statement: no PHI leaves EU, no model weights or inference artifacts go to US for those workloads. Also want a list of subprocessors and whether any telemetry might cross borders. 
[00:55] Naomi: Noted. From product side: Redwood supports regional tenancy — you can pin a project to eu-west-1 and all inference requests are routed to that region. But we also have background telemetry and optional analytics that by default may go to our hosted control plane in the US unless disabled. 
[01:18] Peter: OK, can that telemetry be disabled? We can't assume anything. 
[01:22] Samira: Yes — telemetry can be disabled at the tenant level; and we have a data processing addendum option that prohibits cross-border telemetry for pinned tenants. There's also an option to anonymize telemetry before it's sent out. 
[01:36] Maya: What about model downloads or weights — we heard sometimes model loads happen from a central registry that may be in the US. We need guarantee that models serving EU requests will have assets stored in the EU. 
[01:50] Samira: Good point. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can ensure model artifacts are stored in-region. For Hosted customers on the standard plan, most curated model variants can be cached regionally; but you might see initial pull from central storage. We can provide an SSE S3 bucket in EU or a CDN with EU origin for your tenant. 
[02:12] Arjun: So we need to document which plan gives a strict guarantee — sounds like Dedicated or Private does. 
[02:19] Jordan: Correct. Hosted can be configured but the contractual guarantee is stronger with Dedicated/Private. We'll highlight these tradeoffs in the DPA. 
[02:28] Lina: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? We need BYOK with HSM-backed keys to meet our encryption policy. 
[02:35] Naomi: Yes. We support bring-your-own-key via an integration with common KMS providers. For Hosted we offer a managed KMS or a customer KMS option (we can integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or a Cloud HSM). For Private deployments you can control keys entirely on-prem. 
[02:51] Peter: If we use BYOK in EU, are key operations happening in EU or proxied through US? 
[02:58] Samira: Key operations occur in the region of the KMS by default; we don't route key operations through the US. If you provision an EU KMS, operations remain in EU. We will provide a diagram during the KMS deep dive. 
[03:11] Arjun: About contractual stuff — do you offer EU SCCs or other standard contractual clauses? 
[03:16] Jordan: We have a DPA with SCCs available; we can include the Schrems II supplementary measures we use and a subprocessors list. We'll send the DPA and SOC2 Type II. 
[03:25] Maya: SOC2 — is your SOC2 report US only or audited for EU controls as well? 
[03:31] Jordan: It's a standard SOC2 Type II performed by an external auditor. We'll share the report redacted as needed. It covers security, availability, and confidentiality controls. 
[03:40] Peter: About audit logs — we need immutable logs for access and inference events, retention for 7 years, and ability to export to our SIEM in real time. Can you meet that? 
[03:52] Samira: We have audit logs for authentication, API calls, and admin actions. Retention default is 90 days in the hosted plan, but we offer extended retention add-ons and can stream logs to customer S3 or a syslog endpoint. 7 years is long — for Hosted we'd recommend pushing to your S3 for long-term retention; for Dedicated/Private you can retain locally per policy. 
[04:17] Lina: Do logs contain input text? That's a concern — we often can't store PHI in logs. 
[04:22] Naomi: We can redact or hash input text before storing in logs. Also telemetry can be configured to exclude prompts; audit logs can be configured to log metadata only (request IDs, user IDs, timestamps). 
[04:36] Arjun: Cross-border processing — what about model tuning or reranking workflows where a human reviewer might be in the US? Do you have subprocessors who process customer data? 
[04:46] Jordan: We limit human review; by default we don't do human-in-the-loop on customer data unless explicitly requested. Subprocessors list includes cloud infra providers (AWS, GCP) and monitoring vendors; we will share the subprocessors list and which regions they operate in. 
[05:01] Maya: If we pin to EU, can you guarantee that your support engineers will not access actual payloads from outside EU? 
[05:10] Samira: Support access can be scoped. We have role-based access controls (RBAC) and granular SSO (SAML/SCIM) integrations. We can restrict support access to metadata only for EU-pinned tenants unless you opt into deeper support. Also all access is logged. 
[05:26] Peter: SLA and legal — we need to confirm the contractual warranty around data residency; it's a blocker for procurement. 
[05:33] Jordan: We'll flag that in the DPA. For Dedicated/Private we can add a residency warranty; for Hosted we offer best-effort plus DPA controls and a specific residency section. 
[05:44] Maya: Any public page listing EU regions you operate? 
[05:48] Jordan: Yes, our docs list region availability. We'll link the EU region pages and provide a tenant-level config guide for pinning. 
[05:55] Arjun: A nuance: inference can be routed to EU but some control plane operations, model telemetry, or billing might still go to US. We need explicit list of those. 
[06:07] Naomi: Understood — we'll produce a cross-border processing spreadsheet that enumerates which operations occur where and mitigation (encryption, anonymization, opt-out). 
[06:18] Samira: One technical detail — we do prefix caching and KV cache for prompt speed. That cache may be stored on disk in-region if pinned, but initialization may touch central services for model metadata. We'll show that in the architecture diagram. 
[06:33] Maya: For regulated data in the EU we need to ensure no PII/PHI persists in any backup snapshots that leave region. 
[06:40] Samira: For Dedicated/Private, backups are regionally scoped; for Hosted, we can configure tenant-level backup policies and give you export controls. We'll put this in the DPA. 
[06:52] Arjun: What's the mechanism for region pinning? API flag? Console setting? 
[06:57] Naomi: It's a tenant-level flag: when creating a project you set region=eu-west-1. That setting becomes an enforced routing policy. For existing tenants we can migrate resources to the EU and provide a migration plan. 
[07:11] Peter: If a resource is pinned to EU but capacity in EU is saturated, will requests failover to US? That's unacceptable. 
[07:19] Samira: We have configurable fallback policies. For strict residency we can set 'no-fallback' so requests will queue or fail rather than failover. For business continuity you can opt in to a 'geo-fallback' policy with explicit consent. 
[07:34] Maya: Can you provide an audit trace proving that a request processed in EU only? 
[07:39] Jordan: Yes we produce request-level metadata with region, host IP, and processing node ID. That can be exported and matched with your logs. 
[07:48] Arjun: Encryption in transit and at rest — standard TLS and AES-256? Are there FIPS requirements? 
[07:56] Naomi: We use TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 for at-rest. For FIPS/HSM attestations that's available for Dedicated/Private and via our integration with Cloud HSM providers. We'll document the HSM and FIPS posture. 
[08:11] Peter: About subprocessor geography: are any subprocessors headquartered in the US that process data? We're worried about legal compulsion. 
[08:20] Samira: The main subprocessors are global cloud regions. We can show which subprocessors handle EU tenants and which may process telemetry. The DPA will include SCCs and mitigation. 
[08:32] Maya: Hypothetical: we need end-to-end guarantee that customer prompt text never leaves EU in plain text. What's the recommended configuration? 
[08:41] Naomi: Recommended: (1) pin tenant to EU; (2) provision customer-owned KMS in EU and enable BYOK to control model artifact encryption keys; (3) disable telemetry and analytics; (4) configure audit log redaction for input text; (5) choose Dedicated/Private for contractual residency warranty. That combination provides the strongest guarantee. 
[09:02] Arjun: Good. We'll evaluate Dedicated but need cost numbers. 
[09:07] Jordan: We'll include a cost sketch with the DPA package. 
[09:11] Peter: Can you share a diagram showing network flow, where keys live, and where logs are exported? 
[09:18] Samira: Yes, that's part of the follow-up. We'll include diagrams for Hosted (best-effort), Dedicated, and Private. 
[09:24] Maya: A few quick questions on support: if we need Redwood SRE to debug, will they have to route data outside EU? We need a process where we can approve access or provide sanitized repro. 
[09:36] Naomi: You can approve elevated access workflows. For EU-pinned tenants we default to metadata-only access; you can grant time-limited access to anonymized payloads for debugging. All accesses are logged. 
[09:49] Arjun: For encryption keys, who holds the key for BYOK? We need key rotation policies and ability to revoke keys and render data inaccessible. 
[09:58] Samira: With BYOK you hold the KEK (key encryption key) in your KMS. We support rotation and revocation semantics. If you revoke, you can render data unreadable unless keys are restored; we'll document rotation frequency and emergency key procedures. 
[10:14] Maya: What about European data residency certifications — do you have any EU-specific audits or ISO certifications? 
[10:20] Jordan: We are pursuing ISO 27001; some customers require it. Our SOC2 is complete. We'll surface roadmap on ISO and any regional attestations. 
[10:28] Peter: Latency implications — will pinning to EU add overhead? 
[10:33] Samira: Minimal. Inference nodes in-region avoid cross-border hops. Cold starts for model pulls might add a bit if artifacts aren't cached in-region. We'll talk through warm caches and pre-warming in the demo. 
[10:46] Maya: Regarding subcontractors — any data scientist partners who may do tuning or evaluation? 
[10:51] Jordan: We have a small security review team but we do not use external data scientists on customer data without explicit consent. Model tuning is on aggregated or synthetic data unless contracted otherwise. 
[11:02] Arjun: Let's talk about billing metadata — invoices and usage data sometimes contain hashed ids; where are those stored? 
[11:09] Naomi: Billing data is stored in our billing system, which is currently in the US. We can provide a contractual clause to limit PII in billing records and/or provide anonymized reports for EU customers. We'll include options in the DPA. 
[11:25] Peter: Can we get an exported list of region pinning config options and API flags? 
[11:30] Jordan: Yes, we'll attach the tenant config docs and an example API call for region=eu-west-1. 
[11:35] Arjun: A practical question: if we shift some workloads to Dedicated, how long does a migration take? 
[11:41] Samira: Depending on model artifact size and dataset, 1-4 weeks typical. We'll put a migration checklist in the follow-up. 
[11:49] Maya: Anything else about data residency that is often missed? 
[11:53] Naomi: Two things — telemetry and backups. Always ask where backups and snapshots live, and whether anonymization is sufficient for your policy. Also double-check subprocessors that might sit in the middle (CDNs, logging vendors). 
[12:06] Jordan: Let's open for questions from Atlas. 
[12:09] Peter: Regarding real-time log streaming to our SIEM — do you support TLS mutual auth for log endpoints? 
[12:15] Samira: We support secure syslog, TLS with client certs, and direct S3 deliveries with server-side encryption. Mutual TLS is supported for dedicated log endpoints. 
[12:26] Arjun: Can you show sample audit record fields? 
[12:30] Naomi: We'll include a sample schema: timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, region, node_id, user_id, operation, response_code. We will show that input_text is optional/omitted. 
[12:44] Maya: In terms of regulatory concerns we have to map data flows for DPIAs. Will you help provide a data flow diagram? 
[12:52] Jordan: Absolutely; we'll provide a data flow diagram and narrative for DPIA. 
[12:58] Arjun: About subprocessors' notifications — how do you notify customers about new subprocessors? 
[13:03] Jordan: We notify via email and post to a subprocessors page; high-impact changes trigger direct outreach and require customer approval for certain enterprise plans. 
[13:14] Peter: Anything about EU-US data transfer frameworks we should know? 
[13:19] Samira: We rely on SCCs and technical measures (encryption at rest, BYOK) until new adequacy frameworks are formalized. We'll include the legal basis in the DPA. 
[13:32] Maya: OK, let's talk timelines: procurement wants the legal docs this month. Can you get the DPA and SOC2 by Friday? 
[13:38] Jordan: We'll try to get redacted SOC2 and a DPA draft by 2025-03-14. Is that sufficient? 
[13:44] Arjun: That works; we need the subprocessors list with region mapping. 
[13:48] Jordan: We'll include a spreadsheet. 
[13:51] Samira: For the demo, I'll show an EU-pinned tenant handling PHI-like sample data and show logs exported to an EU S3 and key ops in Azure Key Vault EU. 
[14:02] Lina: Great. Also please show how to disable telemetry via the console. 
[14:07] Samira: Will do. 
[14:09] Peter: A Quirk — sometimes model metadata (not inputs) is pulled from a central service; can that leak model provenance? 
[14:16] Naomi: Model provenance is metadata; we can mirror metadata into your EU origin for pinned tenants. We'll include replication details. 
[14:27] Maya: Any red flags about subprocessor laws in Switzerland, Norway, etc? We have entities across EU and EEA. 
[14:34] Jordan: We'll map by country in the subprocessors spreadsheet and flag data transfer boundaries. 
[14:41] Arjun: Can Redwood sign to notify us ahead of time for new subprocessors that may process EU data? 
[14:48] Jordan: On enterprise plans we can add a notice period. We'll surface the exact clause for review. 
[14:55] Maya: OK, who will we contact if we find a policy mismatch during procurement? 
[14:59] Jordan: I'll be your point; copy Samira and Naomi. For legal touchpoints, I'll include our legal contact in the next email. 
[15:06] Peter: For the audit trail proving region-only processing, can you provide a sample export and retention confirmation? 
[15:12] Samira: Yes — sample export will be in the follow-up packet. 
[15:16] Naomi: Quick note about edge cases — embeddings or model outputs cached in third-party CDNs might be replicated; we'll show how to disable CDN replication for EU-pinned tenants. 
[15:31] Maya: That's important. 
[15:33] Arjun: One last bit — we need an escalation contact for security incidents. 
[15:38] Jordan: We'll include a dedicated incident response contact and expected SLAs for incident notification (72 hours/24 hours depending on severity). 
[15:47] Maya: Thanks. Anything else from Redwood? 
[15:50] Samira: Nothing else. We'll prepare the artifacts. 
[15:53] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll send the DPA, SOC2, subprocessors list, region pinning docs, and the demo link. 
[15:59] Maya: Thanks, talk soon. 

Recap: Action items reviewed and owners assigned. Next meeting: KMS deep dive week of 2025-03-24 (TBD).

End of transcript.
